title: Apply for a small bar liquor licence
summary: This page provides information and requirements for applying for a small bar liquor licence in NSW.
intro:
If you want to operate a small bar in NSW, you'll need to apply for a small bar liquor licence.

A small bar licence allows you to sell alcohol for consumption on the licensed premises, but does not allow gaming.

This liquor licence allows a maximum of 120 customers on the premises during authorised trading hours.

For up-to-date liquor licence guidelines, resources and tools visit Liquor & Gaming NSW liquor licensing.

If you have questions or feedback about liquor licensing contact Liquor & Gaming NSW.
what_you_need: A OneGov account or a MyServiceNSW Account.
Details of the proposed licensee, the premises, and the business owner.
A floor plan clearly showing the boundaries proposed for the small bar (see How to submit a floor plan with licence application – PDF).
A copy of your local council development approval or consent (if applicable).
A completed applicant declaration – PDF (if applicable).
A completed Licence conditions form: small bar – PDF (if applicable).
Evidence of your Responsible Service of Alcohol (RSA) qualification, including Licensee and Advanced Licensee training (if applicable).
A current NSW Police Check certificate issued within the last 3 months.
The 3 identity documents used when applying for the National Police Check.
A current Australian Securities and Investments Commission (ASIC) extract.
The names and birthdates of all directors and office holders (if it is a proprietary company).
A completed appointment of manager notice.
Before applying, check with the local council if you need to lodge a new development consent application.
If applying as an individual, you will need additional documents.
If applying as an organisation, you will need additional documents.

how_to_steps.text: Log in or create an account.
Follow the prompts to complete your application.

more_info.text: Some liquor licence applications require you to notify stakeholders and the local community about your application once it has been submitted.
Find out more about notification requirements at Liquor & Gaming NSW.

Conditions apply to NSW liquor licences. Some conditions apply automatically depending on the type of premises. Other conditions may be imposed on a licence by Liquor & Gaming NSW or the Independent Liquor & Gaming Authority.
Where there are conditions that may be applied, you can include the conditions form with your application. It may help reduce application processing time.
Find out more about licence conditions at Liquor & Gaming NSW.
You can tailor your licence to meet your needs by applying for authorisations and exemptions, for example extended opening hours and takeaway liquor sales.

In certain circumstances you may be eligible to apply for an interim small bar authorisation (ISA). The ISA allows you to begin trading 2 days after you have informed NSW Police and your local council when you wish to operate, and after you've lodged your licence application with Liquor & Gaming NSW.
For more information about authorisations, visit the Liquor & Gaming NSW small bar licence page.

faqs.q: What does a small bar liquor licence allow me to do?
faqs.a: A small bar licence allows you to sell alcohol for consumption on the licensed premises, but it does not allow gaming.

faqs.q: What is the maximum number of customers allowed with this licence?
faqs.a: This liquor licence allows a maximum of 120 customers on the premises during authorised trading hours.

faqs.q: Who is eligible to apply for this licence?
faqs.a: You must be 18 years or older.
